newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil port strike no immediate threat for coffee.
newsitem.headline: Brazil port strike no immediate threat for coffee.

text.p: Brazilian coffee exporters were watching a strike at the key port of Santos but said the stoppage had come at a quiet time for coffee shipments and would only impact on coffee if it continued beyond a couple of days.

"Shipments have fallen substantially in June. If the strike carries on for only two or three days, it will have zero impact," said Jorge Esteve, president of the Brazilian Coffee Exporters' Association, based in Santos.
The strike involves only 800 administrative portworkers who are protesting against not being consulted about the port's switch to 24-hour operations, due to have begun on June 30.

As the workers are responsible for monitoring loading and unloading as well as providing technical assistance, the stoppage has partially paralysed the port, hitting sugar and soymeal loading operations.
Five container vessels docked in public berths have also been affected although it is not known if any of these were taking on coffee.
There is no forecast for an end to the dispute although negotiations are taking place at the local labor tribunal.
The strike has come at a quiet time for coffee shipments after several months when exports exceeded expectations.
Esteve estimated that June shipments should be around one million 60-kg bags and that July and August should also see similar-sized exports.
"It will be in September, October and November that Brazil will ship big volume," Esteve said.
The president of Brazil's Coffee Exporters' Federation, Oswaldo Aranha, said he believed June shipments may not even reach one million bags but that July exports could be nearer to 1.5 million bags.
Aranha also said that the strike would not have an impact on coffee if it was of short duration.
"If you look at the record of port strikes in Brazil over the last few months, they don't last long," he said.
Santos is Brazil's key coffee exporting port.
According to today's bulletin from the Rio de Janeiro Coffee Center, 570,126 bags of coffee had been loaded onto ships at Santos out of a total 741,221 bags throughout Brazil between June 1-27.
